Class JavaFile

java.lang.Object
be.imgn.gaia.processing.source.JavaFile
public final class JavaFile extends Object
A Java source file: a package, one top-level type, and the imports they need, which are worked out when the file is written.

A type is imported unless it is in java.lang or in the package of the file, and written by its simple name. It is written fully qualified instead when its simple name is ambiguous: when two referenced types share it; a type or type variable declared in the file has it; a member type inherited by a type of the file has it, as far as Type.alwaysQualifiedNames() tells; a static import names a member with it; or it is one of the always qualified names. The types declared in the file are written by the shortest name that refers to them where they are used, such as Builder rather than Outer.Builder inside Outer.

Code that refers to a statically imported member through its type, as $T.MINUTES, is written with the member alone, MINUTES.

Files are values: two files written the same are equal.

    • writeTo

      public Path writeTo(Path directory) throws IOException
      Writes the file under a source root, as <directory>/com/example/Foo.java for com.example.Foo, in the current default charset. The folders of the package are created as needed, and an existing file is replaced.

      The file cannot tell which types its package declares, so a type of java.lang that one of them hides, such as Override next to a com.example.Override the file does not refer to, is written by its simple name. Name such types with JavaFile.Builder.alwaysQualify(String...).

      Parameters:
      directory - the source root
      Returns:
      the file written
      Throws:
      IOException - if the folders cannot be created or the file cannot be written

    • writeTo

      public Path writeTo(Path directory, Charset charset) throws IOException
      Writes the file under a source root, as writeTo(Path) does, in a charset. The compiler must then read the file with the same -encoding.
      Parameters:
      directory - the source root
      charset - the charset
      Returns:
      the file written
      Throws:
      IOException - if the folders cannot be created or the file cannot be written, as when the charset cannot encode a character of the source: UnmappableCharacterException

    • writeTo

      public void writeTo(Filer filer, Element... originatingElements) throws IOException
      Writes the file through the filer of an annotation processor, in ASCII only: every character after U+007F is written as a Unicode escape, so that the code means the same under any -encoding of the compilation.

      GeneratedSources writes a file this way too, and also adds @Generated, qualifies the types of java.lang that a type of the package hides, and writes the same file only once.

      Parameters:
      filer - the filer
      originatingElements - the elements the file is generated from, so that incremental builds regenerate or delete it when they change
      Throws:
      IOException - if the file cannot be written, as a FilerException if it was already created
